Alex / team — reviewed Acme’s markup. Below are legal’s recommendations and redline text snippets we should offer back. I’ve included reasoning so sales/procurement can set expectations with the customer.

Summary of position:
1) Output ownership: we can accept that Acme owns outputs that are produced solely from Acme-provided prompts and data ("Customer Content"). We should resist assignment of outputs derived from the model generally or from mixed inputs (model + customer) unless additional consideration is provided. Proposed clause: "Customer retains title to Outputs that are solely generated from Customer Content and prompts; Redwood retains title in Model Improvements and Outputs generated from non-customer content."

2) Training / model improvements: offer a training opt-out limited to the customer’s Customer Content for a defined period (e.g., 12 months) and covered environments. This requires an operational control (see Priyom’s checklist) and a documented onboarding. Proposed clause: "Customer may elect, at onboarding, to prevent Redwood from using Customer Content for training Model Improvements for a period of 12 months following production use; such election will be captured in the Order Form."

3) Feedback license: propose a narrow license for diagnostic/ops purposes that expressly excludes use for model training. Proposed clause: "Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, revocable license to use feedback (telemetry, error reports) solely to operate and improve service quality, excluding training of general-purpose models."

Evidence: require SOC2 report (or equivalent) and written contact for security point-of-contact. If Acme wants output assignment beyond Customer Content, that is a commercial exception and should go to Sales leadership for trade-off.

Redline attached: Proposed_Amendments_Acme.docx (contains the above language). If we can agree to the above, Legal is comfortable with a limited training opt-out and narrow feedback license.

If Acme insists on broad assignment or a full training ban indefinitely, escalate to deal exec for commercial consideration.

— Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Quick ops notes / constraints:

- Hosted API: we can honor a training opt-out on a per-account basis by toggling telemetry capture and preventing data persistence into training pipelines. That requires a documented onboarding flow, ACLs, and a flag in account config. Cost: small infra & monitoring lift; no technical blocker.
- Dedicated pools / Private: easier to guarantee (customer-managed models or air-gapped). If Acme wants guaranteed non-use for training forever, only feasible with Private deployment or contractual controls + audits.
- Evidence required: SOC2 Type II latest report, security contact, and (for private) network architecture diagram.
- Timeline: ops and infra team needs 2 weeks from signed order to implement opt-out and run verification tests for hosted. If they want immediate opt-out upon sign, we can schedule a short blackout period to validate.

Checklist for procurement response (to include in reply):
- Confirmed wording (from Legal)
- Delivery option: Hosted with opt-out (2-week activation) vs Dedicated/Private (longer lead).
- Evidence: SOC2_report_2024.pdf or equivalent.
- DocuSign/implementation links and proposed call time.

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2025-047

Sara / Acme legal — thanks for the redlines and quick turnaround. We’ve pulled together a recommended compromise across Legal and Ops (summary below) and attached a tracked-changes file for review (Proposed_Amendments_Acme.docx).

Proposal summary: 
- Outputs: Redwood will assign title to Outputs only when they are generated solely from Customer Content and prompts. Outputs that materially incorporate Model Improvements or non-customer training data remain Redwood’s. (See tracked language.)
- Training opt-out: Acme may elect an opt-out for use of Customer Content in training Model Improvements for an initial 12-month period post-go-live. For Hosted, opt-out activation requires a 2-week operational onboarding window. For Dedicated/Private, we can agree to stronger non-use commitments with audit-friendly controls.
- Feedback license: Redwood requests a narrow non-exclusive license limited to diagnostic/ops purposes and expressly excluding training for general-purpose models.

Requested evidence / next steps:
1) Please send SOC2 report (SOC2_report_2024.pdf is fine) and security POC.
2) Review the attached Proposed_Amendments_Acme.docx and indicate acceptance or call out the specific lines that remain blocking.
3) If you accept the above, we’ll issue a final Order Form with the opt-out flag and a 2-week activation schedule for Hosted.

Propose a 30-min call Thurs 3/6 at 10:00 AM PT to finalize language if that works for your team.
